title: Short-circuit gopush when marshaled state is byte-identical
description:
`gopush` (`go/state.go:202`) goes straight from `s.Data()` into `s.data.patcher.patch(newBytes)` with no cheap equality check first. When nothing changed, that still costs a full unmarshal of the whole state into `map[string]any` plus a recursive `objectDiff`, only to produce `{}`.

## Fix

Before calling `patch`, compare `newBytes` against `s.data.bytes`; if equal, skip the patch/diff entirely and leave `version`, `delta` and `patcher.prev` untouched (they are already correct by construction).

Watch the existing special cases: the `null` clear path, and the `s.data.bytes == nil` → `{}` seeding on first push.

## Impact

Measured on rais-main: ~3.7 `gopush`/sec, of which only ~2.1/sec produce a delta — so **~43% of cycles are pure waste**. Each wasted cycle is ~10.9 ms and 34,942 allocations; `bytes.Equal` on the same 342 KB payload is 0.016 ms and 0 allocations (**678x cheaper**).

Smallest change with the highest leverage of the three — a couple of lines.
